items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: We've got a Bill Gallaty plays now. Plays a trombone. Yeah, that's his son.

ctx.x: Which one was the leader, Tink? Did you remember him? Bill Gallaty. Bill Gallaty.

Old man, not because he's got a son. We've got a Bill Gallaty plays now. Plays a trombone. Yeah, that's his son. Well, that's his son. He's worked with our band from time to time. Well, that's his son. Well, he's daddy. Because they used to own a dairy. He used to be a dairyman. He used to own a dairy. See? Well, that's all that I could think of. And then, following that was Jack Lane's band. And from Jack Lane's band was Frankie Christian, which I happened to play with them too. I played with Autumn. I kept on…

Well, the reason I ask, Tink, is that every once in a while somebody comes, usually somebody from up north somewhere that is an expert of one kind or another. And I've even had some of them actually tell me that until even around 1920, in the early 20s, that nobody ever heard of any white people playing jazz. And, of course, not having been around myself, I have no personal experience, but it didn't sound right to me. That's why I wanted to ask you.
